card.title: Vector Algebra — Types, Addition and Scalar Multiplication

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A vector is magnitude **with** direction; its length is √(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²) and its direction is captured by the unit vector **â = a/|a|** (NEB 2024: (2î − 3ĵ + 6k̂)/7). **Addition** obeys the triangle law — head-to-tail — equivalently the parallelogram diagonal, and inherits commutativity, associativity, and inverses from it. **Scalar multiplication** scales by |λ| and reverses for negative λ.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - |a| = √(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²); â = a/|a|; |λa| = |λ||a| - a + b: triangle law (head-to-tail); parallelogram diagonal from common tail - AB = b − a; internal division m:n: (n a + m b)/(m+n); external: (m b − n a)/(m−n);…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Writing |a + b| = |a| + |b|; this holds only when a and b are parallel and point the same way.  ·  Treating a zero component as an undefined direction ratio; it simply means the direction cosine in that axis is zero.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Position vectors are measured from the origin; displacement vectors are differences of position vectors.  ·  A negative scalar multiple reverses direction, which is why braking is a negative acceleration vector.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The crossed weights*** — internal division 2:3 gives (3a + 2b)/5: the ratio member multiplies the opposite endpoint, and the midpoint case m = n collapses the formula to (a+b)/2.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: NEB 2024 (unit vector of 2i - 3j + 6k), NEB 2022 (internal division 2:3) — assigned to this row. Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Compute five vector sums and scalar products  ·  Find unit vectors for three given vectors

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: |a| from Pythagoras in 3D; divide by it for the unit vector. AB = b - a. Internal m:n: cross the weights. External division: same crossing with a minus.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Find the unit vector in the direction of a = 2î − 3ĵ + 6k̂. (3m)** — **Step 1 — magnitude:** |a| = √(2² + (−3)² + 6²) = √(4 + 9 + 36) = **√49 = 7**. **Step 2 — unit vector:** â = a/|a| = **(2î − 3ĵ + 6k̂)/7**, i.e. (2/7)î − (3/7)ĵ + (6/7)k̂.…  ·  **NEB 2022 (verified PYQ): The position vectors of A and B are a = 2î + ĵ − k̂ and b = î − 3ĵ + 2k̂. Find the position vector of the point which divides AB internally in the ratio 2:3. (3m)** — **Section formula (internal, m:n = 2:3):** p = **(n a + m b)/(m + n)** = (3a + 2b)/5 — note the crossed weights.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For section-formula answers, state the formula before substituting — the crossed-weights step carries the method mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Vectors add like displacements: head-to-tail bookkeeping is the triangle law, and every algebraic property of addition is a consequence of it.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Vector: magnitude + direction; |a| = sqrt(a1^2+a2^2+a3^2); unit vector a-hat = a/|a|; zero vector has no direction. Triangle law: a + b runs from a's tail to b's head; parallelogram law: diagonal from common tail. Addition is commutative and associative; a + (-a) = 0.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The section formula is coordinate geometry in disguise: the same crossed-weights rule works for plain coordinates (x, y, z) because position vectors are coordinates wearing arrows.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Show that vector addition is commutative using the parallelogram law.** — Draw vectors **a** and **b** from a common tail O. The **parallelogram law** says a + b is the diagonal from O of the parallelogram with sides a and b.…

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: If a = (1, 2, −2), then |a| is → B  ·  For any vectors a and b, |a + b| is always → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Quantities With Direction A **vector** carries magnitude *and* direction; a **scalar** carries only magnitude. The theorems of this topic: the **triangle law** of addition, the **parallelogram law**, and the **section formula** for position vectors — the grammar that every later vector result builds on.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Representation and magnitude - Vector **AB** = position of B minus position of A; written **a** or **AB** with arrow. - **Magnitude (modulus):** |a| = √(a₁² + a₂² + a₃²) for a = a₁î + a₂ĵ + a₃k̂. - **Unit vector:** â = a/|a| — same direction, length 1. **Zero vector 0** has magnitude 0 and no defined direction.…  ·  ## 3. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why vectors add head-to-tail - Displacements compose: walking a then b lands you at a + b. The triangle law is bookkeeping for displacements; the parallelogram law is the same fact seen from a shared tail.…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Scalars vs vectors** | Basis | Scalar | Vector | |---|---|---| | carries | magnitude only | magnitude + direction | | examples | mass, speed, work | force, velocity, displacement | | addition | ordinary | triangle/parallelogram law | | multiplication by scalar | — | stretches/reverses |

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **AB = b − a, not a − b:** the head minus the tail — reversing the order flips the vector.  ·  **λa reverses only for negative λ:** magnitude scales by |λ|, direction by sign.  ·  **Section formula weights:** internal m:n gives (n a + m b)/(m+n) — the weights are crossed, not parallel.
